doc.title: Art Farmer — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: David Monette, the horn maker
summary: Monette in Portland makes horns for orchestral players; Farmer has played the flumpet since about 1990.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Cornet or trumpet: choosing and owning horns

blocks.x: It’s a guy named David Monette, and he’s located out in Portland, Oregon. He comes here to New York City a lot. He’s a real nut for Mahler symphonies. Mahler uses trumpets a lot. He travels all around just to hear those symphonies. He’s a good friend of Wynton Marsalis also. Basically, he makes horns for classical players, like the Boston Symphony, Chicago. The principal players all play his horns. He doesn’t make any real money, but he says as long as he’s able to fly around where he wants to go, it’s okay with him.
Is he making his own mouthpieces for his instruments?
Yeah, he makes his own mouthpieces too.
So, this is your instrument of choice now?
If I look on this album that’s going to be released next, it’ll say, “Art Farmer – flumpet”?
How long have you been playing the flumpet?
The one I have now, I’ve been playing this since ’92, so let’s say since ’90 I’ve been playing the flumpet.
